basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 13.' and it opens 'Vers. 13. Homines Sodomitae pessimi erant et peccatores | coram Domino. Nam et coram'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 13. Homines Sodomitae pessimi erant et peccatores | coram Domino. Nam et coram hominibus pessimi erant. Coram Deo peccator est, qui coram hominibus utcunque justus apparet. Unde et de Zacharia et Elisabeth dicitur: Erant justi ambo coram Domino Deo suo (Luc. I, 6)
